_comment: Synthetic Chrome Trace fixture for test-sycl-gap-device-split.py. Hand-built,
Three device0/compute events, k1 -> k2 -> k3, producing exactly two gaps:
k1->k2  node_idx is EQUAL (1 -> 1).  This is the dispatch-latency floor
calibration case the verdict's B floor rests on: dnode_median must
come out 0.  gap=3,000,000 ns, submit(k2)=4,500,000 puts A at
2,500,000 (clamped inside the gap) and B at the remaining 500,000.
k2->k3  node_idx differs (1 -> 5, dnode=4).  gap=3,000,000 ns,
submit(k3)=8,700,000 puts A at 2,700,000 and B at 300,000.
No sycl.submit events and no ggml.op nodes are included -- hostn stays 0 on
both transitions, which is deliberate: this fixture is only about the A/B
device-clock split, not the host-clock columns.
